attempts.label: DANDI:001545
attempts.paper_title: Diversification of dentate gyrus granule cell subtypes is regulated by Nrg1 nuclear back-signaling
attempts.entry_title: Dentate granule cell subtypes and the Nrg1 V321L mutation (Rajebhosale et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Only the finding that granule and semilunar cells lose their electrical differences in the V321L mutant held in these recordings. The wild-type differences in resting potential, spike width and downstroke went the paper's way but were not significant (p = 0.08 to 0.35), and the separation of wild-type cell types by PCA and a trained classifier also failed. The morphology, soma position, Golgi and RNAScope findings could not be tested because those data are not in the dandiset. The sequencing findings on Penk+ cells and pseudotime could not be tested either, because the kept nuclei and cluster labels are not deposited and the pipeline needs R. The embryonic expression of the semilunar-cell genes held, judged by eye on Allen atlas images.
attempts.description: Tests the electrophysiological findings of Rajebhosale et al. (2025) on dandiset 001545, which holds whole-cell current clamp recordings of 48 dentate granule cells (GCs and semilunar granule cells) from 5 wild-type and 5 Nrg1 V321L mice. It compares the resting potential and spike shape of the two cell types in each genotype and repeats the paper's LDA, k-means, PCA and classifier analyses. Soma positions, morphology, histology and the snMultiome data are not in the dandiset.

Median RMP WT GC -75.3 mV (13 cells), WT SGC -83.8 mV (9 cells), in the paper's direction; two-tailed Mann-Whitney U = 32, p = 0.083 (paper U = 26, P = 0.02). Welch's t test gives p = 0.044, and the exact p is 0.082. The missing 14th WT GC cannot explain the failure. Added above every cell, the best case for the claim, it gives U = 32, p = 0.055 (exact 0.053). Per mouse, the two mice with both types and more than one SGC (VV317, VV326) have SGC medians 1.6 and 2.1 mV below their GC medians; VV256 gave 7 GCs and no SGC, VV318 2 SGCs and no GC. If the 10 pA bias current stored in every sweep was injected, the baselines sit 1.1 to 8.5 mV (10 pA times the input resistance) above the true RMP; removing that offset gives medians -79.2 and -85.4 mV and p = 0.125.
deviations: The dandiset holds 13 WT GCs and 9 WT SGCs where the paper has 14 and 9; which WT GC is missing is not known.

outcomes.notes: The criterion's two readings disagree, and it says to block in that case. On the 18 z-scored features (a) the WT GC mean LD1 is 1.97 and the other groups -1.43 to -0.33, and spike width has the largest LD1 coefficient (3.01, then downstroke -2.88), as the paper says. On the top 9 PCs (b) WT SGC is the group apart (1.67, the others -0.74 to -0.26) and the largest coefficients mapped back to the features are spike amplitude, AHP amplitude and sag (-0.48 to -0.43). The match of reading (a) is fragile. With the AHP width left out and all 48 cells kept, WT SGC is the group apart under both readings (so that variant would be not reproduced), and without mouse VV253 WT GC is apart under neither (reading (a) puts WT GC at 1.16 and WT SGC at 1.37, against -1.49 and -0.46). Question for the paper's authors (recorded as a methods_unavailable finding). Was the four-class LDA of Fig 2M fitted on the z-scored features or on PCs, as the classifier of Fig S2G is? The Methods' LDA section describes only the classifier (scale, prcomp, top 9 PCs, caret lda).

The V321L centroids are 0.86 apart and inside each other's ellipses under both readings, as the claim says for V321L. So the V321L half holds and the WT half does not. The stat_ellipse type "t" ellipse, which is ggplot2's default (the claims file calls the normal ellipse the default; asked in questions/001545.yaml), gives the same (WT squared distances 1.50 and 0.70 against 9.47 and 7.96). outcomes.notes: WT centroids on LD1 GC -0.87, SGC 1.31 (distance 2.18), boundary 0.40. V321L centroids GC -0.10 and SGC 0.07 with their own scaling (distance 0.17, 0.08 of WT), or -0.47 and -0.17 with the WT scaling (0.30, 0.14 of WT). The distance condition holds; both V321L centroids lie on the WT GC side of the boundary, and of the midpoint boundary (0.22), so the side condition does not. The criterion requires both conditions and gives no partial rule, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after verification). The classifier it rests on is at chance on held-out WT cells (figs2g), so the small V321L distance carries little weight. With the AHP width left out and all 48 cells kept, and without mouse VV253, the distance ratio is 0.02 to 0.26 and no V321L centroid pair lies on the WT SGC side.

outcomes.notes: Over 100 random stratified five-fold splits, WT pooled out-of-fold accuracy median 55.0% (35.0 to 75.0) and kappa 0.12 (-0.33 to 0.49); the mean over folds also 55.0%. Always predicting GC would give 60%. V321L with its own scaling 41.7% (kappa -0.11, confusion GC 6 right 4 wrong, SGC 4 right 10 wrong), with the WT scaling 45.8% (kappa -0.01). Neither the four values nor the two accuracies are within tolerance under any reading, and WT accuracy exceeds V321L accuracy by 13.3 or 9.2 points, under the criterion's 15. With the AHP width left out and all 48 cells kept (22 WT, 26 V321L), WT accuracy is 50.0% (kappa 0.02, majority class 59.1%) and V321L 46.2% or 42.3%. Without mouse VV253, WT accuracy is 47.1% (kappa -0.06, majority class 52.9%) and V321L 50.0% (kappa 0.00) or 54.2% (kappa 0.14), the latter within tolerance of the paper's V321L values, but WT stays far from 78%.

GEO GSE280167 holds, per mouse, the raw multiome feature-barcode matrix (342,506 to 501,480 barcodes, every barcode Cell Ranger saw) and, for ATAC, a smoothed cut-site track. The criterion rests on the paper's R pipeline (Seurat with scDblFinder doublet removal, harmony integration, clustering over 41 resolutions and a hand-curated merge into final clusters, Rcode_20230522.txt in RajNINDS/V321L-snMultiome at c124726), whose packages cannot be installed in this entry's locked Python environment. The nuclei it kept and its cluster labels (the GC clusters 0, 1, 5 and 18) are not deposited, so a Python re-analysis would substitute its own cell calling and clustering for the paper's. Not attempted.

The answer does not bear on the block (no fragments, and R tools outside the locked environment), so the claim stays blocked as before; a later attempt that can run it should take VV as WT.

Tested after verification (it was blocked as other, not attempted). The Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas holds one E18.5 ISH series per gene, all sagittal (Penk 100055886, Scg2 100083699, Nrg1 100057764, Cit 100077439). The criterion is a reading of the images by eye. Penk labels a band of cells along the dorsal (outer) edge of the dentate crescent in all three sections shown (45, 52, 59), and Nrg1 a dense band along the same edge (26, 33, 47). The atlas alignment puts the Scg2 crops off the crescent, so its two sections (29, 43) are also shown recentred by eye on their own crescent. There section 43 shows a band of labelled cells along the dorsal edge and section 29 a faint band with a few labelled cells; the expression mask covers 0.0032 and 0.0010 of the recentred crops (0.0008 in the off-centre section 29 crop), against 0.0123 for Penk and 0.0072 for Nrg1. Scg2 labels other regions strongly (whole-brain expression density 0.043). Cit (27, 41, 48) shows sparse, faint labelled cells along that edge (mask 0.0007). The criterion has one condition, labelled cells at the dorsal border for each of the four genes, and no partial rule, as for figs2f; all four meet it, Scg2 and Cit faintly, so the outcome is reproduced (changed from partially reproduced in round 3). The outcome rests on locating the dentate gyrus by eye, as the atlas does not annotate it at E18.5, and on a judgement by eye. Which images Fig S9C shows is asked of the paper's authors (methods_unavailable finding).
deviations: The Allen data are identified by their section data set ids and read through the Allen API; they have no DOI or versioned release to pin.

Assumed. The dentate gyrus is located by eye on Penk section 52 (image 101094568, pixel 3200, 2080), mapped to the E18.5 reference with the atlas's image_to_reference service and from there to each series with reference_to_image; the E18.5 annotation draws only the medial pallium, so no annotated location exists. The overviews in the notebook show where each crop lies. For Scg2 the alignment lands off the crescent, so its sections 29 and 43 are also cropped at a centre placed by eye on their own crescent (pixels 3450, 1900 and 3330, 1730).

Three sections per gene are shown, those nearest the dentate point and 150 um to either side, at 2 um per pixel, and the middle one at full resolution with the atlas's expression mask (display choices).

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the current clamp recordings. The soma positions and the morphology from the biocytin fills (splay angle, branch points, dendritic length, 15 parameters), on which Fig 1F to I, Fig 2C to H, Fig S1 and the multiple regression rest, are not in it, and neither are the Golgi and RNAScope data; 23 of the paper's 56 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

The files hold 13 WT GCs and 9 WT SGCs, where the paper's electrophysiology has 14 and 9, and 12 V321L GCs and 14 V321L SGCs, where the paper has 10 and 15. Nothing in the files says which WT GC is missing or why the V321L cell types differ, so the paper's cell sets cannot be rebuilt.
Every CurrentClampStimulusSeries stores the current in picoamperes (values -60 to 300) under the unit amperes with conversion 1.
The electrode cell_id is VP neuron in all 48 files, though the cells are dentate granule cells.

The general stimulus field says neurons were kept near -65 mV with a constant current and stepped from -60 to 200 pA. The voltage before the steps is -68 to -89 mV in every cell, 14 cells were stepped to 250 or 300 pA, and the bias_current attribute is 10 pA in every sweep, so whether a holding current was applied, and how much, cannot be told. Every sweep of every file also stores the same bridge balance (20 MOhm) and capacitance compensation (1 pF), which look like defaults.

The genotype is coded only as VV or LL in the subject ids; the surgery field says VV is wild type and LL the valine-to-leucine mutant, and GEO agrees, but the cell type is given only as the end of the session description (semilunar or not semilunar), with no column or field of its own.

Question for the paper's authors. Was the four-class LDA of Fig 2M and Fig S2C fitted on the z-scored features or on principal components, as the classifier of Fig S2G is? The Methods' LDA section describes only the classifier. On this dandiset the two give different groups apart on LD1 (WT GC on the features, WT SGC on 9 PCs).

Question for the paper's authors. Which twenty features were extracted, and how were cells with a missing feature handled in the LDA, k-means and PCA? The Methods cite Kim et al (2024), Fig S2C lists eighteen, and the linked code returns twenty-one. Here 4 cells lack the code's AHP width and were dropped, which fits the 21 WT and 23 V321L cells of the Fig S2G matrices.

Question for the paper's authors. Which Allen Developing Mouse Brain ISH series and sections does Fig S9C show for Penk, Scg2, Nrg1 and Cit at E18.5? The atlas holds one sagittal E18.5 series per gene; in those, Penk and Nrg1 label cells along the dorsal edge of the dentate crescent clearly, and Scg2 and Cit only faintly.

GEO GSE280167, where the paper deposited the snMultiome data, holds the raw feature-barcode matrix of every barcode per mouse (genes and peaks) and a smoothed ATAC cut-site track per sample. The nuclei kept after filtering and doublet removal, the cluster labels the paper's snRNA-Seq figures rest on, and the per-nucleus ATAC fragments are not deposited.

disagreements.reason: Penk and Nrg1 clearly label cells along the dorsal edge of the dentate crescent, and Scg2 and Cit show a faint signal there. The criterion has only one condition and no partial rule; for figs2f the author ruled that such a criterion cannot give a partial outcome, and figs9c should follow the same rule. The author's own words, "few distinct labelled cells", describe labelled cells being present, which reads as reproduced with the faintness stated, or as not reproduced if the author judges those cells absent. For Scg2 the alignment lands off-centre (both ML offsets map to section 29, where the crescent fills only the right part of the frame), so the Scg2 mask fraction of 0.0008 partly measures tissue outside the dentate gyrus and should not be set beside Penk's 0.0123 as like for like. The README row does not say that the outcome is assumed.

entries.name: 001545-rajebhosale-2025
entries.title: Dentate granule cell subtypes and the Nrg1 V321L mutation (Rajebhosale et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the electrophysiological findings of Rajebhosale et al. (2025) on dandiset 001545, which holds whole-cell current clamp recordings of 48 dentate granule cells (GCs and semilunar granule cells) from 5 wild-type and 5 Nrg1 V321L mice. It compares the resting potential and spike shape of the two cell types in each genotype and repeats the paper's LDA, k-means, PCA and classifier analyses. Soma positions, morphology, histology and the snMultiome data are not in the dandiset.
